```python
import copy

# Original nested settings
settings = {
    "database": {
        "host": "localhost",
        "port": 5432,
        "credentials": {
            "user": "admin",
            "password": "secret"
        }
    },
    "debug": True
}

# Deep copy before editing
settings_copy = copy.deepcopy(settings)

# Now mutate the copy safely
settings_copy["database"]["host"] = "production.db.com"
settings_copy["database"]["credentials"]["password"] = "new_secret"
settings_copy["debug"] = False

# Original is unchanged
print(settings["database"]["host"])  # "localhost"
print(settings["database"]["credentials"]["password"])  # "secret"
print(settings["debug"])  # True

# Copy has the new values
print(settings_copy["database"]["host"])  # "production.db.com"
print(settings_copy["database"]["credentials"]["password"])  # "new_secret"
print(settings_copy["debug"])  # False
```

**Why `deepcopy`:** A shallow copy (`copy.copy()`) only copies the top level, leaving nested dicts/lists still pointing to the original. `deepcopy()` recursively copies the entire tree, so mutations never leak back.
